highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 adds a new Vulkan/Silk.NET package and expands platform support to Nano Server and container targets.
highlights_body: A new `SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET` package brings Vulkan surface integration. Nano Server gains font rendering via FreeType. Performance and memory fixes round out the release.

bullets.detail: Adds a new NuGet package that wires up a Vulkan rendering surface through the Silk.NET abstraction, with Vulkan tests now running on Android and Linux.

bullets.lead: Nano Server font support via FreeType
bullets.detail: Font rendering on Windows Nano Server now works by using FreeType as the font backend, resolving a long-standing gap where no fonts were available on that minimal image.

bullets.lead: Containerized test coverage for Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, and Nano Server
bullets.detail: CI now validates SkiaSharp on Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server container images, ensuring the library works correctly across these lightweight runtime environments.
All .sln solution files have been converted to the new .slnx format, aligning with modern .NET SDK tooling.

bullets.lead: Memory leak fixed in SKImage.Create raster failure path
bullets.detail: A CoTaskMem pixel buffer was not freed when the native raster image creation failed, causing a memory leak on every failed call to SKImage.Create.

bullets.lead: Eliminated unnecessary string allocation in GetEncodedText
bullets.detail: The null-terminated text path in GetEncodedText no longer creates an intermediate string, reducing allocations in hot text-rendering loops.

bullets.lead: SKRuntimeEffectUniforms lookup map pre-sized at creation
bullets.detail: The internal uniform lookup map is now allocated at the correct capacity up front, avoiding repeated rehashing when a runtime effect has many uniforms.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: FreeType-based font support for Windows Nano Server, fixing a long-standing gap in font rendering on minimal Windows container images
